A source without a version fails too. | | What you see | failed image:NAME: image NAME: expected version X, the source gives Y; the tag is not moved. compose status shows version conflict: want=X source=Y. | | Details | Builds and versions | An image version that the daemon already has with other content also fails the build. unpack reports such a conflict as a failed import. An entity that is in use | | | | --- | --- | | Case | up changes an agent that runs an iteration, or a queue with open tasks. | | Decision | up does not wait. A new image is pending until the next iteration. A harness change restarts a running agent in the start phase and ends its iteration. Every other agent setting applies from the next iteration. A queue bound to a new workflow version keeps its started tasks on the version they pinned. | | What you see | changed agent:NAME. compose status shows image pending until the agent adopts the image. | | Details | Entities that are in use, When the settings apply | An entity removed from the file | | | | --- | --- | | Case | You remove an agent, a group, a task queue, a pool, an env key, a secret or a trigger from the file. | | Decision | up never deletes. The entity stays on the daemon unchanged. compose down before you edit the file, or a direct command, removes it. | | What you see | compose status and up --dry-run list the entities that are tied to the file as not declared. These lines are not drift. | | Details | Removing an entity from the file, What up does not change | A second up | | | | --- | --- | | Case | You run up again on a file that the daemon already matches. | | Decision | A setting that matches makes no call. up refreshes each git Store and builds each path image and each workflow again, because it cannot tell whether a local source changed. A build of unchanged sources gives the digest that the daemon has. An image from a Store builds only for a new image version. up re-provisions only a stopped agent that compose down left without its image tree. A stopped agent that has its image, such as one with loop.enabled: false, stays stopped and gets no call. | | What you see | Each resource is ok, and the summary is 0 changed. | | Details | A second up, How up converges | The first up after down starts an agent with loop.enabled: false and stops it again, because a re-provision always starts the loop. The agent can start an iteration between these two calls. Secrets | | | | --- | --- | | Case | A queue or an agent needs a secret. | | Decision | The file holds only the secret name and its from env variable. compose reads the value from its own environment when it writes the secret. An empty variable counts as not set. A secret that is missing on the daemon and not set in the environment fails its queue or agent. up never removes a secret. | | What you see | The value never appears in the output of up, up --dry-run, status, pack or unpack, in an error, or in a compose archive. status shows secret KEY ok (value not compared) or MISSING. | | Details | Secrets, Agent secrets | After unpack, a secret reaches the target daemon only if its from env variable is set in the environment of unpack. Preview with --dry-run | | | | --- | --- | | Case | You want to see the plan before you apply it. | | Decision | up --dry-run and unpack --dry-run read the live state with GET requests only. They do not start the daemon, build, refresh a Store or write. | | What you see | The plan by phase, the not declared entities, and dry-run: N resources to change, M ok; nothing applied. Env and secret values are not printed. A build, a Store refresh and a Store version show as planned, because a dry run cannot know their result. | | Details | Preview with --dry-run | Versions | | | | --- | --- | | Case | The file names the tariboy versions that it works with, or an archive comes from another daemon version. | | Decision | tariboy: {min, max} holds inclusive SemVer bounds. Every verb that calls the daemon, pack and unpack included, reads the daemon version first and stops before any change when it is outside the range. validate compares the range with the CLI, and with --daemon also with the daemon. unpack and validate --archive also refuse a daemon or a CLI that is older than the producer version of the archive. | | What you see | compose up: daemon version 0.109.0 does not satisfy tariboy = 0.110.0 in /work/Tariboycompose.yaml. The daemon does not change. | | Details | The tariboy version range, unpack | The version of a workflow or image entry is a different check: see A version conflict. Migration from version: 1 | | | | --- | --- | | Case | You have a version 1 file. | | Decision | A version 1 file works as before. To use tariboy, stores, workflows, or an image path, store, source, tag or version, declare version: 2. In version 2, write an image context as path, and declare each agent image and queue workflow in the file. | | What you see | A version 1 file with a version 2 key fails with an error that tells you to declare version: 2. An empty workflows: {} from an older team export is accepted. | | Details | Version 1 and version 2 | Older archives and the archive and import verbs | | | | --- | --- | | Case | You have a team archive from an older compose archive, or scripts that call compose archive or compose import. | | Decision | compose archive and compose import stay for one release as deprecated aliases of pack and unpack, with a warning. compose unpack also accepts a version 1 team archive and sends it to the team import of the daemon. The CLI does not write team archives any more. | | What you see | A deprecation warning on standard error. For an old team archive, the team import preview, then the import after --yes or a y answer. | | Details | Older archives and the archive and import verbs | To move such a team with its images, apply the old archive, then run compose pack with the compose file of the team.
description: What tariboy compose does in special cases - a partial failure, an unavailable Store, a version conflict, an entity in use, a removed entity, a second up, secrets, dry-run, versions and migration.
title: Compose decisions

content: This page is the reference for tariboy compose. It gives a complete file, the fields of each section, the phase order, and the verbs. The Compose page explains how each part works. The Compose decisions page gives the behavior in special cases, such as a partial failure or a secret. A complete file This version 2 file uses every section and every field. Every field except version, the source of each Store, workflow and image, image of an agent, and name of a queue is optional. The parser is strict: an unknown field in any section is an error. scripts/compose-e2e.sh applies a file of this form to an isolated daemon (see Development). Fields by section The "Phase" column names the phase of compose up that applies the field. See Phase order. Top level | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | version | 1 or 2 | Required | All | Version 2 adds tariboy, stores, workflows and the image source fields. See Version 1 and version 2. | | tariboy.min, tariboy.max | SemVer | No bound | Before any phase | Inclusive bounds. min must not be greater than max. See The tariboy version range. | stores | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | git | URL | None | stores | https://HOST/PATH only, without a user, a password, a query or a fragment. Exactly one of git and path. | | ref | Text | The default branch | stores | A branch, a tag or a commit. Valid only with git. | | path | Path | None | stores | A directory. A relative path starts at the directory of the compose file. | See Stores. workflows | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | path | Path | None | workflows | A directory with Workflowfile.yaml. Exactly one of path and store. | | store | Name | None | workflows | A key of stores. | | source | Name | The entry key | workflows | The workflow name in the Store. | | tag | latest or SemVer | latest | workflows | The tag that a queue binds. | | version | SemVer | Not checked | workflows | The workflow version that the source must give. | The name in Workflowfile.yaml must equal the entry key. See Builds and versions. images | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | path | Path | None | images | A directory with Tariboyfile.yaml. Exactly one of path and store. | | store | Name | None | images | A key of stores. | | source | Name | The entry key | images | The image name in the Store. | | tag | Text | latest | images | Any image tag except . and ... | | version | SemVer | Not checked | images | The image version that the source must give. | | context | Path | None | images | Version 1 only. In version 2, use path. | task queues The key is the queue prefix. | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | name | Text | Required | queues | | | description | Text | Keep the live value | queues | An empty value keeps the live value. | | owners | Agent names | Keep the live value | queues | An owner can be outside the file. | | responsible agent | Agent name | Keep the live value | queue bindings | Must be a key of agents. | | pools | Map of pool name to agent names | None | queue bindings | Each agent must be a key of agents. | | workflow | NAME, NAME:TAG, STORE/NAME or STORE/NAME:TAG | No binding | queue bindings | In version 2, NAME is a key of workflows. See Queue workflows. | | triggers[].pattern | Sender | Required | queue bindings | For example plugin:telegram or plugin: . | | triggers[].correlation key | Text | None | queue bindings | | | triggers[].action | create task | create task | queue bindings | | | env | Map of key to text | None | queues, and queue bindings for CUSTOMER AGENT POOL | See the key rules below. | | secrets.KEY.from env | Variable name | Required | queues | The variable of the compose process that holds the value. | An env or secret key holds letters, digits and underscores. It does not start with a digit or with TARIBOY . A key is env or a secret, not both. See Task queues and pools. agents The key is the agent name. If the file omits a field, up keeps the live value. | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | image | NAME[:TAG] | Required | agents | A bare name means NAME:latest. In version 2, NAME is a key of images. | | group | Group name | No group | groups | Must be a key of groups. | | harness.type | claude, codex, opencode, cursor | The daemon default | agents, restart in start | | | harness.model, harness.effort | Text | Keep the live value | agents | An empty value keeps the live value. | | harness.interactive | Boolean | false | agents | Set only when the file has a harness block. | | plugins | Plugin names | The plugins of the image | agents | The exact list. Compared as a set. | | env | Map of key to text | None | agents | | | env mode | merge or replace | merge | agents | replace removes every key that the file does not declare. | | secrets.KEY.from env | Variable name | Required | agents | The key rules of queue secrets. A key cannot be in env too. | | cwd | Path | The directory of the compose file | agents | $CWD and $HOME expand. | | create cwd | Boolean | false | agents | true lets the daemon create cwd. | | user prompt | Text | Keep the live value | agents | Compared exactly. | | alias, notes | Text | Keep the live value | agents | An empty string clears the value. | | color | #rrggbb | Keep the live value | agents | An empty string clears the value. | | messages batch, messages max queue | Whole number, at least 1 | Keep the live value | agents | | | mail instant senders | Agent names | Keep the live value | groups | [] refuses every agent. | | retention.keep iterations, retention.keep days, retention.max bytes | Whole number, at least 0 | Keep the live value | agents | 0 means the daemon default. | | budget.limit usd | Number, in US dollars | 0 | agents | | | budget.period | Duration | 24h | agents | | | budget.mode | warn, block or enforce | warn | agents | enforce is the same as block. | | goal.enabled | Boolean | Keep the live value | agents | | | goal.wait customer timeout, goal.delivery cooldown | Duration in whole seconds | Keep the live value | agents | | | loop.enabled | Boolean | true | agents, start in start | false stops the agent. | | loop.interval, loop.timeout | Duration | Keep the live value | agents | | | timeout | Duration | Keep the live value | agents | The older form of loop.timeout. If both are set, loop.timeout is used. | | loop.hard timeout | Duration, at least 0s | Keep the live value | agents | | | loop.ai stall timeout | Duration in whole seconds, at least 1s | Keep the live value | agents | | | loop.on timeout, loop.on error | restart or stop | Keep the live value | agents | | | loop.max idle iterations | Whole number, at least 0 | Keep the live value | agents | 0 turns the idle stop off. | | loop.schedule | RFC 5545 RRULE, optional DTSTART | Keep the live value | agents | An empty string clears the schedule. | See Agent settings for the daemon call of each field, and Agent settings outside compose for the agent commands that have no field. groups The key is the group name. The members of a group are the agents whose group names it. | Field | Type | Default | Phase | Rules | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | lead | Agent name | Keep the live lead | groups | Must be a member of the group in the file. | | budget | limit usd, period, mode | None | groups | The rules of an agent budget. | Phase order compose up applies the file in this order. A phase starts after the phases before it end. 1. stores: registers, checks out and refreshes each Store. 2. workflows: builds each workflow. 3. images: builds each image. 4. queues: creates each task queue and sets its fields, env and secrets. 5. agents: creates or updates each agent. 6. groups: creates each group, assigns its members, sets its lead and its budget. 7. queue bindings: binds the pools, CUSTOMER AGENT POOL, the responsible agent, the workflow and the triggers of each queue. 8. start: starts or restarts each agent that the file enables. The pools, the workflow binding and the triggers of a queue need the agents, so they come after the agents phase. See How up converges. Verbs Each verb reads -f FILE, else Tariboycompose.yaml, else tariboy-compose.yaml in the current directory. "Checks tariboy" means that the verb stops before any change when the daemon is outside the range of the file. | Verb | Flags | Calls the daemon | Changes state | Checks tariboy | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | validate | -f, --daemon, --archive FILE | Only with --daemon, read-only | No | Against the CLI, and with --daemon against the daemon | | up | -f, --dry-run, --no-start | Yes. Starts the daemon unless --dry-run, --no-start or TARIBOY NO AUTOSTART | Yes. --dry-run changes nothing | Yes | | build | -f | Yes | Stores, workflows and images only | Yes | | status | -f | Yes, read-only | No | Yes | | ps | -f | Yes, read-only | No | Yes | | logs | -f, --tail N, member names | Yes, read-only | No | Yes | | start, stop, restart, kill | -f, member names | Yes | The loop of the agents | Yes | | exec | -f, member, prompt | Yes | Runs one iteration | Yes | | rm | -f, member names | Yes | Removes stopped agents | Yes | | down | -f, -v/--volumes | Yes | Removes the agents and groups of the file | Yes | | pack | -f, -o FILE, --no-build | Yes. Does not start it | Stores, workflows and images, unless --no-build | Yes | | unpack | FILE, --dry-run, --yes | Yes. Does not start it | Yes. --dry-run changes nothing | Yes, and the daemon must not be older than the archive producer | | archive | As pack | As pack | As pack | Deprecated alias of pack | | import | --archive FILE | As unpack | As unpack | Deprecated alias of unpack | The command table in Commands lists the same verbs with their help text.
description: A complete Tariboycompose.yaml, every field by section, the phase order of compose up, and every compose verb.

content: The human/CI client (cmd/tariboy) talks to the daemon over its socket. Commands are grouped by noun. The full, authoritative list — generated from the binary — is in the command reference. daemon subcommands (start / stop / restart / status / logs) work even when the daemon is down. | Group | What it does | | --- | --- | | version | print the canonical Tariboy version locally, without a daemon | | daemon | start / stop / restart / status / logs, config get/set, reindex | | image | build, ls, inspect, prompt, rm | | agent | run, ps, inspect, start, stop, restart, kill, rm, exec, screen, send-keys, status show/history, pull | | cp | Upload LOCAL FILE to the shared server directory, or download AGENT:SRC LOCAL DST | | files | upload base64 content to the shared server directory | | loop | enable, disable, interval, timeout, hard-timeout, on-timeout, on-error | | mail | the tmail client in operator mode: inbox, sent, archive, show, send, reply, requeue, close, read, unread, clear | | assessment | ls with --iteration, --task, --agent, --assessor, --image, --image-version, --limit, --history, and show ID: read assessments. ls returns the latest assessment of each iteration and task; --history returns every assessment. add works only in an agent with TARIBOY TOOLS SOCKET | | group | create, assign, inspect, ls, rm | | plugin | install, ls, inspect, logs, rm | | telegram | contributed by the running bundled plugin: configure, chat setup, status | | schedule | ls | | tasks | the ttasks client in operator mode: the same commands, for example queue create and activity | | secret | set, ls, rm | | budget | set, ls, status | | usage / logs / iteration | AI usage/cost, event stream, iteration inspect/logs/ls | | retention / prune | retention policy, prune old iterations | | backup / restore | portable per-agent tar.gz | | user-prompt | get/set the agent's standing user prompt | | registry: push / pull / login | interact with a tariboy-store registry | See the full command reference for every command and a one-line summary of each. tariboy version and tariboy --version are equivalent plain-text forms. Both work without a running daemon. Plugin command groups are declarative and namespaced. The CLI merges validated contributions from the selected running daemon; core help remains usable when that daemon is unavailable, while contributed commands require it. Secret arguments are accepted only through an owner-only file or stdin, never as a token value in argv. See the Telegram setup workflow. Queue pools and triggers are managed with the operator form of ttasks queue pool and ttasks queue trigger, or through the matching REST routes; Compose is the declarative client for pools and the generated OpenAPI describes the raw API. Workflow images are managed with tariboy workflow. See Task workflows and Workflow images. Agent create and update accept --goal-enabled and --goal-wait-customer-timeout-s; their defaults are enabled and 300 seconds. Inspect and list output also reports the daemon-selected read-only current goal task key. File transfer tariboy cp LOCAL FILE streams a local file through PUT /api/files/raw and prints the returned absolute server path. Files are stored beneath $TARIBOY BASE DIR/files, with a unique directory for each upload and a 1 GiB per-file limit. Agents on that server can read the same uploaded file; uploading does not require an agent or write into an agent's working directory. The lower-level tariboy files upload command remains a JSON/base64 compatibility surface with a 16 MiB decoded-file limit. tariboy cp AGENT:SRC LOCAL DST still downloads from the agent's working directory. The former upload syntax cp SRC AGENT:DST and agent push have been removed; use cp LOCAL FILE and the returned shared path instead.
description: The human/CI client that talks to the daemon over its socket, grouped by noun.
title: tariboy (operator CLI)

content: A standalone image registry server (cmd/tariboy-store, internal/storesvc + internal/storeui): stores agent-image blobs plus a SQLite catalog/token DB and serves an HTTP(S) push/pull API with bearer-token auth. Uploads are capped at 256 MiB and are digest-checked and manifest-validated before replacing a published image. Slow clients are bounded by HTTP header and idle timeouts. Flags - --addr — default :8443, - --data-dir — required, - --db, - --tls-cert / --tls-key, - --token-file, - --anon-pull, - --allow-insecure. Operators interact with it via tariboy push / pull / login. It also serves its own store UI (internal/storeui), distinct from the daemon's embedded web UI.
description: A standalone image registry server that stores agent-image blobs and serves a token-authenticated push/pull API.
title: tariboy-store

content: This is the canonical development guide for the repository. README.md is the short entry point; this page owns the detailed workflow, commands, safety rules, and documentation routing. Before changing code 1. Read the user request or current task as the source of truth for scope. 2. Inspect git status and preserve unrelated work already in the tree. 3. Read this guide and the topical documents from What to read for each task. 4. Locate the existing tests and the nearest working implementation pattern. 5. Identify whether the change affects generated output, persisted state, security boundaries, remote hosts, or a running daemon. 6. For behavior changes and bug fixes, reproduce the behavior and add a regression test before changing production code. The root AGENTS.md turns this workflow into repository instructions for coding agents. CLAUDE.md contains additional rationale for the live-daemon and generated-artifact safety rules. Prerequisites The control plane requires Go 1.26 . Use the repository lockfiles for Node and npm dependencies. Install only the toolchains needed for the area you are changing: - Go control plane: Go 1.26, Make, a C toolchain where required by the host. - Fast checks: ripgrep (rg) for the packaging secret-scan contract in make backend-check and make check. Install with apt-get install ripgrep on Ubuntu or brew install ripgrep on macOS; the backend-check job of the pull request workflow installs it. - React UI: Node.js and npm. - Desktop native host: Rust (minimum package version 1.77), Cargo, the Tauri prerequisites, and platform build tools. - macOS packaging: Apple Silicon macOS 12+, Xcode command-line tools, codesign, hdiutil, and the other checks reported by make desktop-mac. - Agent smoke suites: tmux is checked by both make smoke and make full-smoke; the latter adds the interactive terminal cases. - Documentation: Node.js and npm. - Daemon host: tmux, bash, python3, git, npx (Node.js), the tariboy and ttasks links in /.local/bin, and at least one harness. GET /api/daemon/status reports state: error with the missing tools; see Daemon host tools. Coding agents run shell commands directly in their tool shell, which already has the account's profile environment. Do not wrap a command that carries text (a commit message, a pull request body, a task comment or an artifact) in an extra bash -c or bash -lc layer: quotes, backticks and newlines in the text break that layer. Write the text to a file with the Write tool and pass the file (git commit -F, gh pr create --body-file, ttasks ... --file), or use a quoted heredoc at the top level of the command. Keep credentials in the environment; never print their values. Load the Rust environment before Cargo or desktop commands: Do not assume a GUI-launched macOS application inherits the interactive shell's PATH; native runtime dependencies must be handled at the Desktop process boundary. Runtime PATH contract At daemon startup, Tariboy defines the account baseline by invoking the configured shell as an interactive login shell with a fixed internal probe: The probe is not constructed from user input. It has a five-second timeout, bounded combined output, disconnected stdin, and a machine-readable delimiter so startup messages cannot be mistaken for the result. The daemon accepts only an absolute executable shell and a non-empty result without NUL bytes, then sets the resolved PATH before initializing agent, plugin, or HTTP services. Desktop reads the effective macOS account's configured shell and supplies it only to the daemon child. Direct terminal and SSH launches use their inherited SHELL. Desktop's bootstrap path can locate the daemon and common host tools, but it is not the final runtime path. If shell selection or the bounded probe fails, daemon startup remains available with its inherited PATH and emits a stable warning; neither the inherited nor resolved path nor shell startup output may be logged, audited, or included in support bundles. After resolving the account baseline, a packaged daemon prepends its shared runtime bin directory, which contains the ttasks, tmail and tscripts symlinks to the sibling tariboy-tasks, tariboy-mail and tariboy-scripts payloads. This makes the bundled clients available to fresh Desktop agents without the optional CLI installation. Each alias is refreshed atomically and retained across restart handoff. The final iteration environment preserves this precedence: 1. daemon environment, including the resolved account baseline; 2. harness-required environment; 3. explicit agent environment and resolved secrets; 4. for non-bare images, the agent bin directory prepended to the resulting PATH. An explicit agent PATH therefore intentionally replaces the daemon baseline before non-bare agent-bin prefixing. Bare images receive no agent-bin prefix but still inherit the daemon baseline unless the agent overrides it. Harness shell wrappers use /bin/sh -c, not a second login shell, so they preserve the already-resolved environment. The runner validates the selected harness executable against this final environment before it starts the shim. Schema-v2 image skills add only adapter-owned launch arguments or environment entries. They may not override HOME, CODEX HOME, or XDG CONFIG HOME. Repository map | Path | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | cmd/ | Go binary entry points: daemon, CLI, shim, and store service. | | internal/ | Go domain logic, APIs, persistence, loop, mail, proxy, plugins, and embedded store UI. | | ui/ | Shared React/TypeScript source and the Desktop and store UI build targets. | | desktop/src-tauri/ | Rust/Tauri native host, daemon lifecycle, SSH, Keychain, tunnels, support export, and packaging resources. | | /github/tariboy-store/ | Separate repository containing canonical image sources and Agent Skills. | | scripts/ | Isolated smoke, end-to-end, packaging, and release verification. | | docs/docs/ | Current product, operator, architecture, and development documentation. | | docs/releases/ | Release notes and acceptance evidence. | | docs/superpowers/specs/ | Historical and active feature design decisions. | | docs/superpowers/plans/ | Historical and active implementation plans. | Current product and architecture docs take precedence over historical plans. Read a historical spec or plan when extending the feature it describes or when the current docs link to that decision. What to read for each task Always read this page first, then read every row that matches the task. You do not need to read unrelated subsystems. | Task area | Required reading | | --- | --- | | Daemon, API, persistence, lifecycle | Architecture overview and State model | | Iteration loop, harness execution, terminal, tmux | Iteration loop and Shim | | Mail, letters, delivery, events | Mailbox and Mail reference | | AI proxy, usage, budgets, pricing, audit | AI proxy and audit and Security and controls | | React UI and frontend behavior | Web UI architecture | | Desktop native host, SSH, Keychain, tunnels, packaging | Remote hosts, Security and controls, and this guide | | Images and groups | Images and Images and groups | | Plugins and agent tools | Plugins and Binaries | | Release, support, diagnostics | Support, Security and controls, and docs/internal-alpha-release-runbook.md | | HTTP commands, response types, OpenAPI, generated UI types | Command registry, API layer, and API types | If behavior crosses rows, follow all matching routes. For example, a terminal change in the Desktop app requires the loop/shim, Web UI, and Desktop/SSH rows. Build and verification matrix Use the smallest fast entry point that covers the change; the aggregate and heavy targets compose them: Run make backend-check for backend-only changes and make frontend-check for frontend- or documentation-only changes. Run make check for mixed changes or when ownership is unclear. The backend target runs fmt-check, vet, staticcheck, gocyclo, gocognit, test, Go unit tests, desktop-rust-check and smoke contracts. Its test and tariboy-tasks-e2e steps also check the HTTP API against the committed OpenAPI snapshot; see Go control plane and plugins. The frontend target runs the UI format check, the generated API types check, UI typecheck, lint with the complexity and size thresholds, the unused-code check, unit tests, which fail when Vitest finishes fewer test files than it found, the Storybook build (ui-storybook), branding, the bundle budget, and the documentation checks. The documentation step restores the last build from a host cache when no input of the site changed; see Documentation build cache. Before checking, backend-check runs go mod download for the module and for tools.mod. frontend-check uses scripts/npm-ci-locked.sh for locked installs under ui/, ui/tools/api-types/ and docs/. They do not write into bin/ or dirty git status. Each step reports its result and duration as it finishes. Successful check-step output is suppressed; failed steps print their command and complete diagnostics, and every run ends with a compact summary. make full-check is the full set of checks that run unattended on a developer machine, not every check in the repository. It runs check, then build, the five core E2E scripts, full-smoke, the two Playwright browser suites, and one desktop step for the host: desktop-e2e on Linux x86 64, desktop plus desktop-smoke on macOS arm64, and the version and lock gates alone elsewhere. After dependency preparation succeeds, the check steps do not stop at the first failure. Each step is timed and recorded, and the run ends with a summary table naming every step that failed, so one aggregate pass surfaces gofmt drift and a UI type error together. Pull request CI The workflow .github/workflows/pull-request.yml runs for every pull request and for every push to main. It does not run make check as one job. The backend-check job uses three caches: - apt packages. awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action restores the package files on a cache hit and does not run apt-get update. On a miss, it installs the packages and saves the cache. To rebuild the cache, increase its version input. - cargo. actions/cache keeps the desktop-rust-check target directory ( /.cache/tariboy/desktop-check-target, the default of TARIBOY CARGO CHECK DIR) and the cargo registry and git caches. The key contains the Rust version of the runner and the hash of desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock. When the lockfile changes, the job restores the newest cache of the same Rust version and cargo compiles only the changed crates. A new Rust version on the runner starts with an empty cache. - staticcheck. actions/cache keeps /.cache/staticcheck. setup-go caches only the Go build and module caches, so without this cache staticcheck analyzes the standard library and every dependency on each run. The key contains the hash of go.mod, go.sum, tools.mod and tools.sum. When one of them changes, the job restores the newest staticcheck cache. staticcheck checks the inputs of each cached entry, so an old entry is never used for changed code. A pull request run can restore caches of its own branch and of main. The run on each push to main saves the caches that new pull requests use. A cache miss or a failed restore does not fail the job: it installs and compiles everything, as without a cache. Checks on a shared host Several agents can run make check on one host at the same time, and together they can use all memory and disk. The fast checks therefore limit themselves: - Check slot. A top-level check, backend-check or frontend-check run first takes a host-wide lock on /tmp/tariboy-check.lock with flock. Every worktree shares that path, so only one check runs at a time. A second run prints waiting for a check slot (/tmp/tariboy-check.lock) and starts when the first run ends. The wait has a limit of one hour. After that, the run fails with no check slot after 3600s and does not run its steps. A killed run frees its slot. TARIBOY CHECK SLOTS=N allows N runs at a time, TARIBOY CHECK LOCK changes the lock path and TARIBOY CHECK LOCK TIMEOUT changes the limit in seconds. A host without flock, such as macOS, prints check slot: flock not found, running without a host lock and runs anyway. An agent that runs make check with a tool timeout must run it in the background, because the wait counts against that timeout. - Parallelism. When TARIBOY AGENT is set, as it is in every agent session, CHECK JOBS defaults to 2. CHECK JOBS=N adds -p=N to GOFLAGS, unless GOFLAGS already sets -p, sets the vitest worker count through TARIBOY VITEST MAX WORKERS, and passes --jobs N to desktop-rust-check. Without TARIBOY AGENT or CHECK JOBS, nothing changes. Set CHECK JOBS=N yourself to override the default. Vitest uses at least two workers. If TARIBOY VITEST MAX WORKERS is a number below 2, Vitest uses two workers and prints ui-test: TARIBOY VITEST MAX WORKERS=N is below 2; using 2 workers, ... on stderr. One vmThreads worker runs all test files in one VM context, and the run fails. An empty value or a value that is not a number gives four workers. - Memory gate. With two workers, ui-test uses about 1.4 GB of memory at its peak. Before that step, frontend-check runs scripts/ui-test-memory-gate.sh. The script reads MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo. If the value is 1700 MB or more, the script prints nothing and ui-test starts at once. If the value is lower, the script prints memory gate: waiting for MemAvailable = 1700 MB before ui-test (now N MB, limit 600s) and reads the value again every 5 seconds. It prints a progress line once a minute. When the value reaches the threshold, it prints a line with the wait time and ui-test starts. After 600 seconds the script stops waiting. It prints ... is still below 1700 MB after 600s; running ui-test anyway and ui-test runs. The step is never skipped: if memory then runs out, ui-test fails with its diagnostics, and the warning line above it gives the cause. TARIBOY UI TEST MIN MEM MB changes the threshold in MB, and 0 turns the wait off. TARIBOY UI TEST MEM WAIT TIMEOUT changes the limit in seconds. A host without MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo, such as macOS, prints one line, ... has no MemAvailable, not waiting for memory, and does not wait. The wait happens while the run holds the check slot, so other runs wait for the slot for that time too. A direct cd ui && npm test does not wait. - Temporary files. A top-level run creates $TMPDIR/tbc.XXXXXX (or /tmp/tbc.XXXXXX) and gives every step TMPDIR=<run dir /t. Test homes, t.TempDir() directories, Go build files and npm temporary files go there, and the run removes the directory when it ends. Each run writes its process ID to <run dir /pid. A run that was killed cannot remove its directory, so the next run removes every tbc. directory whose process is gone. Test isolation Any test daemon or agent must use its own data directory, runtime directory, and listener configuration. Never stop, restart, reuse, or point test tooling at the user's live daemon, /.tariboy, /.tariboyd, or 127.0.0.1:9990. For an ad-hoc daemon: Remove the temporary directories only after the isolated process is confirmed stopped. The repository smoke and end-to-end scripts already enforce their own isolation. :::danger A second daemon using the live base directory shares the SQLite database and loop managers. It can double-execute iterations, reconcile the same agents, and reap live sessions. Isolation is a data-safety requirement. ::: Go test isolation and speed Go tests follow these rules so the suite stays fast, parallel, and away from live state: - Test databases come from internal/store/storetest. storetest.Open(t) returns a migrated database in a temporary directory, and storetest.OpenAt(t, path) does the same at a given path. storetest.Seed(t, path) writes a migrated file for code that opens the database itself, such as daemon.Run. The first call in a test binary runs the real migrations once; every later call copies that template. Call store.Open directly only to reopen an existing file or to test migrations. - Packages whose tests start a daemon, a loop manager, or the CLI call testutil.IsolateEnv() from TestMain. It removes every TARIBOY variable and points HOME at a temporary directory. The suite passes with TARIBOY RUNTIME DIR and TARIBOY BASE DIR set to paths that do not exist. loop.NewManager never reads the environment: tests pass RuntimeDir (use testutil.ShortDir(t) for socket paths) and may pass BaseEnv. For nested go build commands only, pass testutil.RealHome() as the child process's HOME to reuse Go caches. Keep the test process and built binaries on their isolated HOME. - Wait for state, not for time. Use testutil.WaitFor instead of a time.Sleep loop, and prove that something did not happen with a hook, a fake timer, or testing/synctest. A time.Sleep that must stay in a test has a comment that says why. A test that starts daemon.Run waits on Options.Ready instead of polling the daemon socket. - Mark independent tests with t.Parallel(). Tests that use t.Setenv, os.Chdir, or package-level state stay sequential, also when a helper they call does it. A sequential test has a comment that says why. In internal/tasks and internal/commands every new test calls t.Parallel() unless such a reason applies. - internal/commands tests get a handler through cmdHandler or h. These helpers share one registry for the test binary. BuildRegistry() builds the result schema of every command, so call it only in a test that checks the registry itself. - Tests that drive a real tmux have the tmux build tag (internal/shim/shim tmux test.go). make test adds -tags tmux when tmux is installed, and make vet always vets them. Run them alone with go test -tags tmux ./internal/shim/. Rebuild it through the owning target and inspect the resulting diff for unrelated source or secret material. Change workflow 1. Understand: read the task, this guide, and topical docs; inspect current code, tests, and recent changes. 2. Design or diagnose: agree on behavior before feature work; establish root cause before bug fixes. 3. Protect behavior: add a focused failing test for code changes, or define an executable validation for documentation and scripts. 4. Implement narrowly: preserve unrelated work and avoid opportunistic refactors. 5. Synchronize docs: update operator, architecture, reference, and contributor docs whenever behavior, commands, prerequisites, or boundaries change. 6. Verify: run every relevant row from the verification matrix plus git diff --check. 7. Review: inspect the complete diff for correctness, security, generated files, and scope before committing. 8. Commit: use a focused message and report what was verified. Versioning Ordinary tasks, including code-changing tasks, do not bump the version. Move the canonical version only when cutting a release, by running scripts/set-version.sh NEW VERSION, the single supported mechanism. Hand-editing a pinned version file is not supported. This release-time policy prevents version-pin merge conflicts that previously forced implementation chains to run one at a time. Choose the release version from everything landed since the previous release: - use a patch bump for bug fixes, refactoring, performance work, test-only code changes, build tooling, and other changes that add no user-facing capability; - use a minor bump for new commands, APIs, UI capabilities, or other user-facing functionality; - while the product remains on 0.x, also use a minor bump for an intentional incompatible behavior change unless the user specifies another release decision; - use the highest-impact category when a release includes several changes. internal/version.Version is the canonical full version. scripts/set-version.sh writes scripts/release-version.txt, a second declaration of that value, at the same time and no other mechanism writes it. A disagreement proves the supported mechanism was bypassed and fails the release gate. After make build, verify that ./bin/tariboy version and ./bin/tariboy --version print the exact canonical value; do not use make install merely to put a build on PATH. Definition of done A change is complete when: - the requested behavior and scope are implemented; - focused regression tests and the affected subsystem suites pass; - formatting, lint, vet, or Clippy passes for each changed language; - daemon and agent tests used isolated state; - generated artifacts match their documented Git contract; - current documentation describes the resulting behavior and commands; - release cuts use exactly one appropriate patch or minor version bump through scripts/set-version.sh; - every new documentation link resolves and the docs site builds; - git diff --check passes; - the final diff contains no unrelated edits, credentials, or temporary files; - Important and Critical review findings are resolved.
description: Canonical contributor guide for the Go control plane, React UI, Rust desktop host, documentation, and isolated end-to-end tests.
title: Building, testing & development

content: An image defines the plugins available to an agent, optional packaged Agent Skills, and the exact prompt template rendered for each iteration. Harness, model, effort, interactive mode, environment, policy, and secrets are runtime or compose configuration. They are not schema-v2 image fields. Browse built images In Desktop, open Library → Images (/library/images). The list has one row per image name on the selected host. Version and Built describe the newest tag. Source names the Store that built it, when the provenance says so. Used by counts the agents whose current or pending image is any tag of that name. Run agent opens the New agent dialog with latest, or with the newest tag when the image has no latest. The rows are sorted by Used by , then by name. Show unused is off by default, so images that no agent uses are hidden. The image bare is not listed: the New agent dialog offers it as Plain terminal . The search field filters by name. Newest is selected by parsed built at, not SemVer. Tied dates prefer the matching version tag, then stable tag-name order. Missing or invalid dates sort last. Imported archives keep their original build time, not the import time. The Add image menu has three items: - Build from directory opens the directory build form in a dialog. - Import archive opens the archive import in a dialog. - Get from a source opens Library → Sources . Select an image name to open its newest tag with the Overview, Template, Skills, and Files tabs. Below the Overview, Versions lists the tags with manifest versions, build dates, full digests, the Store, and separate Latest and Newest badges. It shows the newest five tags and Show all N . Current and pending agent usage and Run agent, Export, Upload to servers, and Remove stay on each tag row. Select a tag for its own tabs. The old /servers/:hostId/images/… URLs redirect to the same page under /library/images. Detail reads carry the displayed manifest digest. If a ref changes between reads, the UI reports the update, discards the old content, and reloads once. A further change offers Refresh image , so repeated rebuilds cannot cause an endless refresh loop. The read API accepts optional expected digest on manifest, template, prompt, provenance, file-list, and file-content requests; a mismatched published digest returns HTTP 409 image changed. CLI equivalents accept --expected-digest. Requests without that value retain their existing behavior. Every detail read is serialized with publication, so its digest check and content read describe one generation. Build from an original directory Open Images , enter the directory containing Tariboyfile.yaml, choose a required name and an optional tag, then select Validate or Build . The default build publishes both the source image version and latest, or only latest when the source has no version. An explicit tag publishes only that tag. Tariboy records the canonical source CWD as local provenance and retains a frozen source snapshot for evidence. Rebuilding still reads the original directory and its current paths. Validate is read-only. Before a build it shows the schema version, explicit plugin names, packaged skill metadata, template hash, and every prompt entry in declared order. Static entries include their original source string, resolved category, byte size, and full SHA-256; runtime entries remain named placeholders. Errors block the build. Warnings call out omissions such as identity or finishing instructions, host-bound absolute paths, unusually large prompts, missing obvious plugin instructions, and a static external-plugin version that differs from the active runtime version. Validation never repairs or reorders the template. Use Open in VS Code on an image detail page when the source CWD still exists on the selected local or SSH host. Imported images have no source CWD. New Image creates a managed schema-v2 source from only a name and optional initial prompt. The generated project is prompt-only; edit its Tariboyfile.yaml to declare packaged skills or plugins before building. The equivalent operator command is: tariboy image validate prints its result in full and exits 1 when the source or the target ref is invalid, so a script can stop before image build. Provide --repository-id and --git-commit together when the source is an exact Git revision. Tariboy records those explicit values in the frozen source snapshot; it never infers a commit from the current working directory. For CLI calls, a relative --path is resolved against the shell's current working directory before the request is sent to the daemon. Build as an operation The daemon runs each build in the background as an operation. A build does not block the Web UI, and it does not depend on the request that started it. - In the Web UI, Build shows the notice "Build started" with the link Open operation . The link opens the page of this build under Settings → Maintenance . - The Operations log of Settings → Maintenance lists every image and workflow build of the host, newest first, 50 per page. The page of one operation shows its status, arguments, result or error and its full log. The page of a running operation updates its status and log live. Download log saves the log file. - tariboy image build prints the operation id and the operation log to stderr until the build ends. Then it prints the result as before, for example digest: ..., to stdout. A failed build exits 1 with its error code and message. Ctrl+C stops only the output; the build goes on in the daemon. - tariboy image build --detach prints only operation: ID and exits. - tariboy operation ls [--page N] [--limit M], tariboy operation show ID and tariboy operation log ID [-f] read the operations of the daemon. The log names each build step: the parse of Tariboyfile.yaml, the extends chain, the skills lock restore with the full npx output, the source snapshot, the wait for the image name lock, the layer build, the tags and the provenance record. A failed build ends with its error code and message. A daemon stop interrupts a running build: its operation gets the status interrupted, and the previous image tags stay. Start the build again after the daemon starts. Refs, tags and identity A ref is the stored image content. Its id, also called its digest, is the SHA-256 of the image content. The content lives once in images/<name /refs/<digest .tar.gz, and the manifest field id holds the same digest. A tag is only a pointer to a ref. It is held in images/<name /tags/<tag . The digest is the SHA-256 of this text: - The text has one line for each archive member, manifest.json included. The lines are sorted by path in byte order, and each line ends with a newline. - <mode is the permission of the member as four octal digits, for example 0600 or 0700. - For manifest.json, the body is the canonical manifest: the manifest JSON object without the keys built at, tag, digest and id, encoded again with sorted keys and no spaces. So every change to a skill file, a skill description, a prompt layer, the role, the plugins or the image name gives another digest. The same content gives the same digest, whatever its build time or the member order in the archive. The format is the same for images with and without image version. tariboy image inspect, import and every read of a stored archive calculate the digest again. An archive whose id is not its content digest is refused with image manifest id does not match content digest. Archives built by earlier releases stay readable without a migration: - An archive whose id is sha256(name + "\n" + image version) is a legacy archive. Its digest stays that id, and its content is not checked. - An archive without id keeps the SHA-256 of its archive file as its digest. Agents pinned to a legacy digest keep running. Files and tags on disk are not rewritten. A build never rewrites content that is already stored under its digest. If the same content is already stored, the build only moves the tags. Generations that no tag names stay on disk, so agents pinned to an earlier ref keep running until their next launch gate. For the rule that applies when you rebuild one image version with other content, see Image versions. There is one build mechanism. The operator CLI, the Store build, an agent's own image-creator, and team import all publish the same way and behave identically, including how they default tags. Repeat --tag to move several tags onto one build; every requested tag names the same ref and reports the same digest, so a versioned tag and latest can never disagree. The requested refs and their snapshot/provenance metadata commit as one batch; a failure on any tag restores every tag exactly. Duplicate tags are rejected. When --tag is omitted, a source with image version publishes both that version and latest, and the single-result output reports the versioned ref; a source without a version publishes only latest. Explicit tags, including --tag latest, take priority and do not add another ref. The daemon-managed bare:latest ref is reserved. You cannot build it, import over it, or remove it. basic is an ordinary Store image. You can rebuild, export, and remove basic:latest, also a legacy one without provenance. A store written by an earlier release is migrated once, when the daemon starts: each archive keeps its digest as its ref id, so every digest already pinned on an agent continues to resolve. The migration is one-way. Stores on a server Open Stores beside Images to register a Git repository or an absolute directory on the selected server. Each tariboyd owns its own registrations and performs clone, refresh, and build on that server. A Store contains image sources at images/<image name /Tariboyfile.yaml. Git sources are cloned under <base-dir /stores/<store name /. For a daemon running as agent with defaults, team lives at /home/agent/.tariboy/stores/team/, and its reviewer source is /home/agent/.tariboy/stores/team/images/reviewer/Tariboyfile.yaml. TARIBOY BASE DIR or the daemon's --base-dir changes that root. The ref of a Git Store A ref is a branch, a tag or a commit of a Git Store. store add --ref REF checks the managed clone out at that ref. store ref NAME REF changes the ref of a registered Git Store, and store ref NAME "" returns it to the default branch of the remote. Without a ref, the Store follows the default branch, as before. Only a Git Store takes a ref. A local Store is your own checkout, so --ref on a local Store returns bad store (HTTP 400). Switch its branch in that directory instead. Tariboy looks for the ref in this order: 1. A branch of the remote. 2. A tag. 3. A commit id of 7 to 40 hex digits. The daemon fetches the remote and finds the commit of the ref before it changes the tree. If no branch, tag or commit matches, the request returns store ref not found (HTTP 400). The tree and the stored ref then stay as they were. store add with an unknown ref registers nothing. A ref that holds a space, starts with -, holds .. or is longer than 255 characters returns bad store ref (HTTP 400) before Git runs. store list, store show and the other Store commands return ref and commit. ref is "" for the default branch. commit is the full id of the checked-out commit, and "" for a local Store without Git. A refresh follows the ref: a branch moves to its newest commit, a tag is read again because someone can move it, and a commit stays the same. The automatic build calls the same refresh, so it builds images from the commit of the ref. The default Store On each start, the daemon registers the public Tariboy Store https://github.com/alekzonder/tariboy-store.git under the name tariboy. It does this only when no Store has the name tariboy or that source, and the daemon did not record a removal. After that, the daemon builds tariboy/basic when no image named basic exists. It never rebuilds an existing basic. Both steps run in the background, so the daemon is ready before they finish. The build is an ordinary operation in the Operations log of Settings → Maintenance . - If you remove the Store with tariboy store remove tariboy, the daemon does not register it again by itself. - If the clone or the build fails, the daemon tries again at the next start or when you run onboarding.retry (POST /api/onboarding/retry). It does not retry on a timer. - onboarding.status (GET /api/onboarding) reports the state of the Store and the starter image. - If TARIBOY ONBOARDING=off is set or the daemon starts with --onboarding=off, the daemon registers and builds nothing at start. If you removed the default Store, Library → Sources offers it again as one button. Add tariboy Store registers https://github.com/alekzonder/tariboy-store.git under the name tariboy on the selected server and opens its card; it is the same request as tariboy store add tariboy https://github.com/alekzonder/tariboy-store.git. The button is hidden when the server already has a Store named tariboy or a Store with that source, and while the daemon still connects the catalog. The form for another Store is under Add another catalog . The server needs HTTPS access to github.com; a failed clone registers nothing and shows the daemon error. A local source such as /srv/company-images is used in place, without a copy. Stores are the source of canonical agent images and skills; the daemon no longer installs a separate built-in Store tree. A Store may also hold workflow sources at workflows/<workflow name /Workflowfile.yaml. Store detail lists them beside images, and tariboy workflow build STORE/NAME builds one; the Store card in Library → Sources lists them under Workflows with a Build button. The official Store provides two: development, the pull request flow (plan, approval, implement, review, complete, done; it needs the GH TOKEN queue secret and a developers pool), and research, one pool status for a researchers pool that produces a report artifact. See Workflow images for the operator sequence. Automatic refresh and build A Store can refresh and rebuild itself on a schedule. tariboy store auto NAME --interval MINUTES --image IMAGE stores a whole-minute interval and the images selected for automatic builds. The Automatic builds disclosure of the Store card in Library → Sources shows the same policy as an interval field and one checkbox per image. An interval of 0 disables it, which is the default for a new Store. Every minute the daemon runs the cycle for each Store whose interval has elapsed: it refreshes that Store exactly as Refresh does, then builds each selected image that reports an update, using the default tags so both <image name :<image version and <image name :latest are published. An image is built only when the source and latest both declare versions and those values differ, so an unbuilt or unversioned image is never built automatically. A failed refresh skips that Store's builds for the cycle, and a failed build does not stop the remaining selections or Stores. Failures are logged and retried at the next interval; missed cycles are not replayed, so a daemon restart can delay a due cycle by up to one interval. Saving a policy restarts the interval from that moment. An automatic build uses only the content of a commit. A manual Build and tariboy image build STORE/IMAGE still build from the Store directory as it is. For each automatic build the daemon: 1. Checks that the Store root is the root of a Git repository: it has its own .git entry, and git rev-parse --show-toplevel returns the Store root. A plain directory or a directory inside another repository fails with store not git. 2. Exports the HEAD commit with git archive into a new owner-only directory under <base-dir /image-build/. Ignored and untracked files of the working copy, for example an old images/NAME/.agents/ or pycache /, do not enter the image. Uncommitted changes do not enter it either. The working copy is not changed. git archive applies the export-ignore and export-subst attributes of .gitattributes; submodule content and Git LFS objects are not exported. 3. Fails the build when the commit has a symbolic link, an extends layer, a skills[].dir or a prompts[].file that points outside the commit. 4. Installs every skills-lock.json in the export, in the order described below for Store builds. 5. Compares each installation directory's .agents/skills/ with the locks installed there, a later lock replacing an earlier entry of the same skill. Each locked skill must be installed, the hash of its files must equal the lock's computedHash, and no other skill may be there. The hash is the one the skills installer writes: sha256 over each file's relative path followed by its content, with files ordered like JavaScript localeCompare and .git and node modules skipped. 6. Builds and publishes the image from the export, then removes the export, also after a failure. A failure publishes nothing: neither the version tag nor latest moves. Every error starts with Store NAME image IMAGE: and names the cause, for example: A lock mismatch has the code skills lock mismatch, a Store without its own Git repository store not git, and a path outside the commit bad store. The daemon log line Store automatic build carries the error, and tariboy store show NAME and GET /api/stores/NAME return the last attempt of each selected image in auto.results: A success records an empty error, so an earlier error disappears. Deselecting an image removes its entry. A Store refresh failure is only logged, because no image is selected for a build at that point. The provenance of an automatically built image (tariboy image provenance REF) records git commit, the full SHA of the exported commit, and lock digest. lock digest is sha256: followed by the hex sha256 of one line per installed skills-lock.json, in installation order: the Store root's lock, then the lock of each extends layer in layer order, or the image's own lock. Each line is <path from the Store root , a NUL byte, the hex sha256 of the file's bytes, and a newline. Without any lock the value is the sha256 of an empty string. repository id stays empty, and source cwd names the image directory in the Store working copy. Because every automatic build installs its skills into a fresh export, the installer downloads remote skills on every automatic build; without network access the build fails and nothing is published. The automatic path is selected by the operation initiator auto, which only the cycle sets. An API client that calls POST /api/images/build with a Store selector and initiator: auto also gets a build from the commit. The registration's name and source are persisted in the daemon database together with this policy (interval, selected images, and the last cycle time). Viewing a Store still reads the current disk inventory and image version values; there is no saved image list to become stale. For each valid source, the detail inspects <image name :latest directly and shows that manifest's image version. It marks an update only when the source and latest both declare versions and those values differ. Missing latest, an unversioned source or latest, and a damaged latest artifact remain distinct states. A damaged latest does not hide healthy siblings or fall back to another tag. A successful Build reloads the inventory and reports both the version tag and latest when the source is versioned. A missing images/ directory shows an empty list. An invalid source reports its own error and disables its Build action while valid sibling images remain available. Refresh of a managed clone makes it match the remote exactly. It runs git fetch --prune --force --tags origin, finds the commit of the Store's ref (the default branch when the ref is empty), then runs git checkout --force --detach COMMIT and git clean -fd. Local edits, local commits and untracked files in <base-dir /stores/<name / are discarded on every refresh. Files ignored by .gitignore are kept. The managed clone stays on a detached HEAD (a checkout of a commit without a local branch). A local Git checkout root, including a Git worktree, is refreshed with git pull --ff-only and its local edits are never reset or stashed. A local directory without its own .git entry is simply reread; Tariboy does not pull an ancestor repository. A fetch, missing upstream, conflict or authentication failure is returned as store refresh failed (HTTP 409) and carries the tail of Git's error output, so the UI and CLI name the cause. For a local checkout, resolve it there, for example after git -C <path status, then refresh again. Remove unregisters the Store and deletes its managed clone; it preserves local source directories and already built images. Store builds use the existing image builder. By default, a versioned source publishes both <image name :<image version and <image name :latest, while a source without a version publishes only latest. Use --name to avoid a name collision between Stores, and --tag to publish only an explicit tag. Do not combine a Store selector with --path. Store Build advances every requested tag atomically after validation. Existing version tags and latest do not require a different target name or tag. The Store page's Build always publishes the defaults; to publish another name or tag, use tariboy image build <store /<image --name NAME --tag TAG. An explicit tag publishes only that ref; other refs remain unchanged. Before freezing sources, the daemon runs npx skills experimental install in the Store root when skills-lock.json exists there, then in the image directory when it has a separate lock. An image with extends instead installs each layer's lock in its temporary assembly directory, in layer order, after the Store root (see Inherit from other images). The installer rewrites skills-lock.json, so the daemon restores each lock file's original content after it runs, including on failure; a build leaves the Store checkout's tracked lock files unchanged and does not block a later Refresh. An installation failure stops the build before publication. Git must be installed on the daemon host; lock restoration also requires Node.js/npm and access to the skill sources. Without npx on the daemon PATH the build stops with building this image requires npx because it has skills-lock.json; install Node.js (npm ships npx) on the daemon host. Private repositories use the server account's configured SSH or Git credential helpers. Configure access on that server before adding the Store; do not put credentials in its URL. In Desktop, Library → Sources shows one card per Store. The card header has the name, the source, the number of images, and a ⋯ menu with Refresh and Remove store… . Each image row has the source image version, one status, and one button: | Status | Button | | --- | --- | | Built | Build (rebuilds) | | Update available (built → source) | Update | | Not built | Build | | Could not read the built image , with Details | Build | | The Store entry is invalid , with Details | none | | Build failed: and the reason, with Open operation | Build | Update available shows only when the two versions are known and differ. This comparison cannot detect changed source bytes when image version stays the same. After such a change, increment image version in the Store source. A build of the same version with other content fails with image version conflict (see Rebuild a version). The Automatic builds disclosure below the tables holds the interval and the images it builds. Built artifacts appear in Library → Images . Stores do not yet expose standalone skills or plugins. Image versions Set image version: 0.1.0 in Tariboyfile.yaml to version the image independently of schema version and the Tariboy product version. Both source schemas accept SemVer 2.0.0, including prerelease and build metadata, without a v prefix. Complete SemVer versions are also valid image tags. Read or increment the version locally, without a running daemon: Both version commands default to ./Tariboyfile.yaml; --path accepts a file or directory. They print only the resulting version (or a JSON string with --json). update major, update minor, and update patch increment that component, reset lower components to zero, and remove prerelease/build suffixes. For example, 1.2.3-rc.1+build.7 becomes 1.3.0 after update minor. Updates atomically replace the file while preserving its permissions, YAML fields, and comments; YAML formatting may change. Missing or invalid versions produce an error without changing the file. Old sources may omit the field for build compatibility, but version commands require it. Rebuild a version One image version names one content. When you rebuild an image, the build compares its content digest with every stored archive of the same name and the same image version. Legacy archives are compared by their content too. - If an archive with the same content exists, the build publishes nothing new. It moves the tags onto that archive. - If only archives with other content exist, the build fails with the error code image version conflict (HTTP 409). The error names the ref, the current digest and the new digest, for example: image reviewer:1.2.0 already exists with digest OLD; this build has digest NEW. Bump image version in Tariboyfile.yaml or rebuild with --force. No file is written and no tag moves. - An image without image version never conflicts. The tag latest alone does not cause a conflict. To roll out a change, increment image version. To replace the content of the version anyway, run tariboy image build --force, or send force: true to POST /api/images/build. The build then publishes the new digest and moves the tags onto it. The old archive stays on disk under its own digest, so agents pinned to it keep running. The operation log of the build gets one line: When several archives are replaced, old digest lists them, separated by commas. Read the line with tariboy operation log ID or tariboy operation show ID, or in Settings → Maintenance → Operations log . Find the build with tariboy operation ls. The log is deleted with its operation when the maintenance retention period ends. The same rule applies to every path that publishes an image: | Path | On a conflict | | --- | --- | | tariboy image build, Build in the Web UI, Store builds and onboarding | fails with image version conflict; --force is available | | Automatic Store builds | the build operation fails with image version conflict; the next cycle tries again; it never forces | | A build by an agent (image-creator) | the tool returns the conflict error | | Build of an editable image source (image.source.build) | fails with image version conflict (HTTP 409) | | Import runnable image and transfer to servers | the import fails and the tag does not move | | tariboy pull | the pull fails and the tag does not move | The tariboy-store server and the daemon-owned bare:latest always publish. The Web UI has no force switch. It shows the conflict error of the operation. The runnable manifest preserves image version; the archive carries no tag, since a tag only points at a ref. Every new iteration snapshots the source version with the ref and digest, exposes it through iteration inspect, and includes it in runtime: identity and iteration audit exports. Older runnable images and historical iterations simply omit the version. Schema version 2 Schema v2 is strict and accepts only schema version, image version, extends, plugins, skills, and prompts: The prompts sequence preserves the order of static files and ordinary runtime values. For every non-bare agent, Tariboy prepends a platform-owned Task Processing Order block containing one-shot, messages, and Goal. Older entries for those inputs are accepted but do not render duplicate sections. Tariboy does not add an identity header or finishing tail. An empty list produces an empty image template, but the platform work block is still rendered at runtime. Each static file is resolved and embedded at build time. Supported forms are: | Form | Resolves from | | --- | --- | | $PLUGINS/... | The common external-plugin root | | ./... | The original directory containing Tariboyfile.yaml | | ../... below a declared skill | That skill's frozen source snapshot | | /absolute/path/... | An operator-supplied absolute filesystem path | The builder expands only those literal variables; it never performs shell or environment expansion. A prompt may use ../ only to read a file below a source-relative directory already declared in skills; validation reads that directory directly and build reads its frozen snapshot. Other traversal, symlinks, missing files, non-regular files, and oversized prompt files are rejected. Inherit from other images with extends extends lists parent image source directories. Each entry uses ./, ../, or an absolute path and resolves from the directory of the image that declares it: The build expands the chain into ordered layers: every parent's own parents first, then the parent, in extends order, with the child last. An image reached twice, such as a shared ancestor, is used once at its first position. A cycle, a missing parent, a parent that is not schema v2, and a chain deeper than 16 images are rejected before anything is built. Tariboy assembles the layers in a temporary owner-only directory under <base-dir /image-build/ and removes it after the build: 1. Each layer's directory is copied over the previous one. A file with the same path is replaced; other files remain. 2. If the copied layer contains skills-lock.json, a Store build runs npx skills experimental install in the assembly directory and then removes the lock. The installer skips a skill whose SKILL.md is already in .agents/skills/, so a skill of the same name installed by an earlier layer stays. An automatic build then refuses the image with skills lock mismatch when the later lock pins other content. 3. Each layer's ./ prompt files are copied to ./.tariboy-extends/<layer /<path , so equal prompt paths from different images stay separate files. The reserved .tariboy-extends directory must not exist in a source. 4. ../ skill and prompt paths are rewritten to absolute paths from the layer's original directory. The lists are then concatenated in layer order. plugins keep the first entry of each name. skills keep the last entry of each skill name, so a child replaces a parent's skill. prompts keep the first entry of each runtime placeholder and of each file content, so a shared ancestor's prompt is not repeated. The child's image version names the result. The merged Tariboyfile.yaml has no extends and is validated, frozen, and built exactly like any other source; Validate shows the merged result. extends works for --path builds, Store builds, and an agent's own image builds. Only Store builds run the per-layer skills installer; for the other builds, restore the lock in each image directory first. Managed image sources and team imports reject extends. A child can only append: it cannot remove an inherited entry or insert a prompt between a parent's prompts. Layering deletes no files except ROLE.md, so a skill directory copied from a parent keeps files the child's copy lacks. Rebuilding a parent does not rebuild its children. Describe the role with ROLE.md ROLE.md is an optional Markdown file that describes what the image is for. Put it next to Tariboyfile.yaml. The build copies its text into the manifest field role. Tariboy does not put this text into the agent prompt, the prompt layers, or the agent directory. The text is metadata for people and for the UI. Write ROLE.md in English. Say only what the role is and why the image exists. Do not describe the process, skills, commands, or rules. The daemon does not check the language or the content of the text. The build applies these rules: | Case | Result | | --- | --- | | No ROLE.md | The manifest has no role field. manifest.json is the same as before this feature. | | Only white space | The same as no file. | | Not valid UTF-8 | The build fails with ROLE.md is not valid UTF-8. | | Up to 500 characters | role.text is the full file. | | More than 500 characters | The build fails. The error gives the file size in characters and the limit of 500. | | A symbolic link or not a regular file | The build fails. | A character is one Unicode code point, so 500 Cyrillic letters are in the limit. A child image built with extends does not inherit the ROLE.md of a parent. Only the file in the directory of the image that you build counts. tariboy image inspect and GET /api/images/{ref} show the field: ROLE.md is not a member of the image archive, but role is part of manifest.json. Thus ROLE.md changes the image digest. Pull, push to a Store, import and the activation of an image by an agent accept role only when the text is valid UTF-8, is not empty, and has 500 characters or fewer. The strict archive check, which runs on import and on activation, also rejects unknown fields in role. A daemon older than this feature does not know the field: its strict check rejects an image with role. Images built before this feature have no role field. Packaged Agent Skills Each skills entry explicitly packages one Agent Skill directory into the image. The skill travels with runnable export/import. At iteration launch Claude Code and OpenCode receive it through native skill configuration; Codex receives a compact prompt catalog with its absolute SKILL.md path and reads the file on demand. This is separate from image plugins and prompt entries; none implies another. See Agent Skills in images for the directory and frontmatter contract, source paths, validation limits, manifest fields, portability, harness adapters, discovery precedence, and activation failures. Runtime placeholders Runtime entries remain visible placeholders inside the built image. Before every iteration, the runner replaces ordinary values at their declared positions. Work inputs are always grouped in the platform block: | Placeholder | Value at iteration start | Skill named in the rendered instruction | | --- | --- | --- | | identity | Current agent name, active image ref and digest, CWD, and iteration identity | whoami | | goal | Compatibility marker; selected Native Task fields appear in Task Processing Order | none; platform-owned | | workdir | Absolute managed agents/<agent /workdir, independent of the effective CWD | workdir | | context | Durable agent context | context | | messages | Compatibility marker; open letters and outstanding requests appear in Task Processing Order; requires the mail capability or its messages alias | none; platform-owned | | awaiting-replies | Compatibility marker; outstanding requests appear under Messages in the platform block | none; platform-owned | | user-prompt | The agent's standing prompt | none; this is task input | | one-shot | Compatibility marker; single-execution input appears first in Task Processing Order | none; this is task input | Each non-empty ordinary runtime value starts with # [runtime: <name ]. For skill-owned values, the short instruction to use that skill follows the heading and names the skill without embedding an installation path. Context data then starts with Agent Context. The platform block starts with # Task Processing Order, followed by a fixed ordering instruction and ## One-shot, ## Messages, and ## Goal. Missing work inputs have explicit empty-state text and an instruction not to search for them with commands. Outstanding replies use a nested ### Awaiting replies heading; message and task content is retained. This grouping applies to existing images without rebuilding and to images without work-input entries or plugins. It grants no additional capabilities or packaged skills. Existing declared markers still undergo normal image contract validation. Each singleton placeholder may appear at most once. Empty ordinary runtime values add no text. The Template tab shows static paths, categories, sizes, hashes, and runtime markers in their exact order without draining messages. External plugins Image-owned static prompts and complete Agent Skill trees come from the image source and are copied into the runnable artifact. Dynamic runtime placeholders and built-in or external plugin implementations remain daemon-owned. External plugins are separate: Versions can exist side by side, while one version per plugin name is active and supervised. Images select plugin names, not plugin versions. Adding a plugin never adds its prompt implicitly; include every required static prompt path in prompts. Assign an image to an existing agent Build the image in Images , then open the agent's Configuration tab and select it under Agent image . The choice is persisted as pending. Tariboy does not interrupt a running iteration: it validates and activates the image through the next iteration's launch gate, then snapshots the image ref, source version, digest, and prompt-template hash for that iteration. Activation changes only image bytes, plugin capabilities, and image-owned shims. It preserves harness, model, effort, environment, interactive and loop settings, CWD, context, workdir, mail, history, audit, and group. A validation or staging failure leaves the current image active and exposes a retryable pending error. The pending selection can be replaced or cancelled before activation. The image tag list shows agent names separately under Current and Pending , so an operator can see both active use and assignments waiting for their next launch gate. An image in either list cannot be removed. Configuration shows Current (or Activated version when stopped) with the version read from the agent's pinned ref and digest. Next iteration previews the explicit pending digest first, otherwise the content the active ref points at now, otherwise the current pinned image. Viewing this projection does not create pending state or activate anything. Inspection and activation errors remain visible even when there is no pending ref; missing version metadata is labelled Version not specified .
